chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, is the visitation of Al-Rida (peace be upon him) superior or the visitation of Abu Abdillah Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'The visitation of my father is superior, and that is because Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) is visited by all people, whereas my father is visited only by the elite of the Shi'a.'

key_terms.زِيَارَةُ الرِّضَا: Visitation of Al-Rida (Imam Ali ibn Musa)

ai.seo_question: Which is superior: visiting Imam Al-Rida or Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that while the visitation of Imam Al-Husayn holds greater merit due to its universal appeal, his own visitation is reserved for the *khawass* (elite) of the Shi'a, highlighting a distinction between general devotion and specialized spiritual intimacy. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that while the martyrdom of Al-Husayn is a global event of redemption, the specific love and knowledge associated with the Imams require a deeper, more exclusive commitment from the faithful. The comparison underscores the unique status of Imam Al-Rida as the 'Pleasure of the Shi'a,' whose recognition is a sign of true doctrinal depth.
